meta.name: experimental-design
meta.description: Design experiments and studies BEFORE data is collected — choosing a design, randomizing, blocking, and laying out treatment combinations so results are interpretable. Use whenever someone is planning a study, asks how to assign subjects/samples to groups, mentions randomization, blocking, stratification, controls, factorial or fractional-factorial designs, design of experiments (DOE), screening many factors, response-surface optimization, crossover or repeated-measures or split-plot designs, cluster/group randomization, Latin squares, plate layouts, batch/run-order effects, replication vs. pseudoreplication, or sequential/adaptive/group-sequential designs. Trigger even for informal phrasings like "how should I set up this experiment", "how do I avoid confounding", "what's the best way to test these 6 factors", or "assign these mice to conditions". For computing the sample size or power once the design is chosen, use statistical-power; for analyzing data already collected, use statistical-analysis.

copy.tagline: 在动手收集数据前,把实验分组、随机化和对照方案设计清楚
copy.fit_line: 适合你,如果正准备做实验却不确定该怎么分组、随机和设置对照。
copy.tagline_en: Design your groups, randomization, and controls before collecting any data
copy.fit_line_en: For you if you're planning a study and need sound randomization and grouping

howto.what: 在收集数据之前帮你把实验设计好:选设计类型、随机分组、设区组、安排因子组合,并用带种子的脚本生成可复现的排布,导出 CSV 文件。也会提醒伪重复、混杂这类结构性问题。
howto.when: 当你规划一项研究、问怎么把受试对象或样本分到各组,或提到随机化、区组、因子设计等时触发;像「这个实验该怎么搭」这类非正式问法也会接管。

say.text: 我要筛 7 个因子,帮我排一个 Plackett-Burman 设计
say.note: 给出运行顺序已随机化的试验表

say.text: 把这 60 名受试者按 2:1 随机分到用药组和安慰剂组
say.note: 输出区组随机化分配表

say.text: 这些小鼠该怎么分配到各处理组?我担心伪重复
say.note: 先说明重复层级,再给分组方案

howto.what_en: Before data collection, Claude picks a design type, randomizes and blocks units, lays out factor combinations, and generates seeded, reproducible allocation or DOE scripts that export CSV files. It also flags structural errors like pseudoreplication.
howto.when_en: Triggers when you plan a study, ask how to assign subjects or samples to groups, or mention randomization, blocking, or factorial designs; informal phrasings like "how should I set up this experiment" also count.

say_en.text: I need to screen 7 factors — set up a Plackett-Burman design
say_en.note: Returns a run table with randomized order

say_en.text: Randomize these 60 subjects 2:1 to drug and placebo
How should I assign these mice to conditions? I worry about pseudoreplication
say_en.note: States the replicate level, then the layout
